title: From two squares to a 12-player party shooter
author: HkingH69
selftext:
The first clip is Block Arena before I used any AI: two squares in Unity, one arena, shoot each other. That took me weeks of learning and implementation.

Six months ago I started working on it with AI, and this is where it is now:

* up to 12 robots a match, 8 of them on one screen, or online with friends over Steam
* 6 modes: Free-for-All, Team Deathmatch, Capture the Flag, King of the Hill, Juggernaut and Gun Game
* 13 arenas, including a lab with portals, conveyor belts and laser gates
* 10 robot skins, power-ups, bots for empty seats, and Windows and Mac playing together

**How AI helped me**

* **Code:** a back-and-forth with Claude/Codex, online multiplayer included. I set the rules, the feel and what's wrong after every playtest; the AI did a lot of the heavy lifting on the implementation.
* **Art:** the robots, arenas, effects and icons are AI image generation from briefs I wrote, and I picked what made it in. Claude for helping me with the briefs and Codex for image gen.
* **Music and sound:** The soundtrack and every sound effect are synthesised in code - the music is a script that renders the WAVs.

**What AI was bad at**

* **Testing:** It can't see the game. Things that looked right in code were wrong on screen - grenades were once drawn four or five tiles long.
* **Voices:** Tried a bunch of announcer voices, robotic and AI, and none felt right. They got replaced with short music stings.

Happy to answer anything about the workflow. It's out on Steam on Nov 6 for Windows and Mac - if you want to follow it, a wishlist helps a ton:

[Hking's Block Arena on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3149210/Hkings_Block_Arena)
